shared_elements: horizontal band or line with a row of short repeated vertical strokes (comb-like)
repeated motifs stacked in parallel horizontal registers
curved/hooked terminal forms (arched shapes above; upturned prow-like ends)
justification: The most specific correspondence is the repeated horizontal band carrying a row of short evenly spaced vertical strokes, which appears both in the upper register of the pillar and in each of the elongated forms on the rock surface, and both compositions stack such banded motifs in parallel registers. Otherwise they differ fundamentally: A is a deep three-dimensional relief dominated by recognisable animal bodies with modelled volume on an upright shaped block, while B is a flat linear outline design of abstract elongated forms with no modelling, scattered over an irregular horizontal rock face.
